what: This file lists the candidate landing regions for Artemis III near the lunar south pole.
It holds the nine regions of the NASA list of 28 October 2024 and the 13 regions of the NASA list of 19 August 2022.
Connecting Ridge is on the 2022 list. The page shows it, thus the file keeps it.
The two lists share six regions. Thus the file has 16 regions.
NASA studied these regions as candidates. NASA did not select a landing site in them.
For each region, the file gives the centre, the source of the centre and how sure we are.
It also gives the NASA 5 m terrain model, if one exists, and the Sun ceiling.
meta.status: Reference list. The pipeline does not read this file. twinfinder/moon.py holds a copy of the centres and boxes of the three regions without a terrain model. The positions of the other 13 regions come from their terrain models. All 16 regions are in the pipeline and on the page (second pass, 15 November 2026).
meta.saved_copies: Copies of the pages and files that we read on 15 November 2026 are in data/raw/lunar_regions_provenance. Older copies are in data/raw/moon_provenance.
meta.page_regions_kept: The four regions of the first build (connecting-ridge, malapert, mons-mouton, nobile-rim-2) keep the centre, the terrain model and the Sun ceiling of data/derived/moon_targets.json without change.

sun_ceiling.meaning: The Sun ceiling is the highest that the centre of the Sun can climb above a flat horizon at a lunar latitude.
sun_ceiling.with_terrain_model: The ceiling uses the latitude of the centre of the model grid. The range uses the most poleward and the least poleward of nine points of the grid (corners, edge centres, centre), as in twinfinder/moon.py fingerprint().
sun_ceiling.without_terrain_model: The ceiling uses the latitude of the centre of the box on the NASA 2024 map. The range uses the same nine points of that box. The file says so for each region.

coordinates.longitude: centre_lon, degrees east, 0 to 360, as in data/derived/moon_targets.json. centre_lon_pm180 gives the same longitude from -180 to 180.
coordinates.projection: South polar stereographic with true scale at the pole and a sphere of radius 1737.4 km, as in twinfinder/moon.py polar_xy_to_latlon. PGDA, USGS and the NASA map use this projection.
coordinates.precision: Values have more digits than their accuracy. Use the how_sure field. A model centre is exact for the model grid. A map centre is good to approximately 1 km.

how_sure_values.from the terrain model: The centre of the grid of a NASA 5 m terrain model (PGDA product 78). For each such region, the USGS box of the 2022 region has the same corners as the model to less than 1 m. For the six such regions on the 2024 list, the box on the NASA 2024 map also agrees to less than 0.2 km. Thus the model and the region are the same box.
how_sure_values.estimated from a map: The centre of the region box on the NASA map of 28 October 2024. We fitted the map to lunar coordinates with six boxes that have a terrain model. The largest error at those six boxes is less than 0.2 km.
not used: from a gazetteer feature of the same name
how_sure_values.note: The USGS table of box corners (an official table) agrees with each model to less than 1 m. We give the model centre and keep the USGS box as a check.

names_2022_to_2024.how_sure: High. The NASA 2024 map draws the 'Mons Mouton' box at the place and size of the 2022 box of 'Leibnitz Beta Plateau' (USGS). The centres agree to 0.02 km. LROC titles its mosaic 'Nobile Rim 1 and Mons Mouton (Leibnitz Beta Plateau)'. NTRS 20250002110 says that the nine regions are six of the 13 and three new regions. No NASA text says 'renamed' in words.
New region. Its box on the 2024 map is north of the Mons Mouton box and approximately 77 km by 58 km.

meta.removed_regions_note: A NASA abstract (NTRS 20250011660) says that the cut to nine regions does not imply that the removed regions are unsuitable for future exploration.

not_confirmed: No NASA page gives a table of centres or of boundaries for the nine regions of 2024.
Three centres (Peak near Cabeus B, Mons Mouton Plateau, Slater Plain) come from the NASA map. LROC mosaics agree for the first two. For Slater Plain, the map is the only source.
No NASA text says in words that 'Leibnitz Beta Plateau' is now 'Mons Mouton'. Two official products show the same box with the two names.
The region boxes (USGS, PGDA, NASA map) are 16 km to 30 km wide. NASA said in 2022 that each region is approximately 15 km by 15 km. Thus a box can be larger than the region that NASA uses.
We did not read the journal paper on the nine regions (JGR Planets, DOI 10.1029/2025JE009434). The publisher refused our request (HTTP 403).

The first pass and the second pass of 15 November 2026 downloaded the nine terrain models of the new regions into data/raw. The pipeline read them for the slopes, the Sun ceiling and the sunlight share.
corrections_to_research_notes: The NASA 2022 list names 'de Gerlache Rim 1'. The notes and the USGS files say 'de Gerlache Rim'.
The 2022 region 'Leibnitz Beta Plateau' is the 2024 region 'Mons Mouton', not 'Mons Mouton Plateau' (target_sites.md, Inferences).
Slater Plain is at approximately 87.16 S, 125.57 E on the NASA map. The value 88.1 S, 127.8 E in the notes comes from a student code project, approximately 29 km away.
Peak near Cabeus B is at approximately 83.64 S, 291.22 E (68.78 W). The notes estimated approximately 83.4 S from a distance in a magazine.
The IAU gazetteer gives the centre of the crater Haworth at 87.45 S, 5.17 W, not 86.9 S, 4 W. The Haworth region is not at the crater centre.
The IAU gazetteer gives 13 May 2022 as the approval date of the name Mons Mouton. NASA announced the name on 15 February 2023 (SVS 5074).

pgda_models_not_used.note: PGDA product 78 also has these models. None of them is a candidate region on the two lists.
models: LM2 to LM6 and LM8: Shoemaker Rim A to F
pgda_models_not_used.site20: Site20 is the 2022 box of Leibnitz Beta Plateau. The page uses Site20v2, which has the same centre and a larger extent.

for_the_pipeline: twinfinder/sun.py ELEV_EDGES_DEG has a bin edge at each of the 16 Sun ceilings (21 bins). A new region needs an edge at its own ceiling, or its limit must fall within LIMIT_SLACK_DEG (0.005 degrees) of an edge.

The stored horizons (data/derived/horizon_cells.json) give the open share at the nine old bins only. Thus the hours after hills are a lower bound for each region with a bin that starts at a new edge. data/derived/grazing_cells.json meta.horizon_bins.hills_exact gives this for each region.
The models Site20v2 (Mons Mouton) and Site06 (Nobile Rim 1) overlap by approximately 12 km by 15 km.
The Haworth model is the largest file (approximately 142 MB). The other new models are approximately 41 MB to 64 MB each.

Three regions of 2024 have no NASA 5 m terrain model: Peak near Cabeus B, Mons Mouton Plateau and Slater Plain. For these three regions, the slope likeness needs another terrain source. We did not check one.

coordinate_source.detail: We read only the header of the GeoTIFF (bounds in south polar stereographic metres). We calculated the centre with twinfinder/moon.py polar_xy_to_latlon.

regions.how_sure_note: The PGDA model and the USGS box agree. The region is not on the 2024 map.

terrain_model.how_matched: The USGS 2022 box for 'de_Gerlache_Rim' has the same corners as model Site11.

regions.sun_ceiling_basis: Centre latitude of the terrain model; the range uses the most poleward and the least poleward latitudes of the model grid, as in twinfinder/moon.py.
